summary: Larose tower at the Larose Forest headquarters near Bourget, Ontario; a 1971 photo caption says it was manned. No build date found.

facts.status_note: No dated source confirms the tower's condition today.

events.note: Photo caption dated circa June 1971 says the tower was manned

evidence.supports: Register: tower located at the Larose Forest headquarters
evidence.quote: Located at the Larose Forest Center Headquarters.

evidence.supports: Forest lies about 60 km east of Ottawa
evidence.quote: It is about 60 kilometres (37 mi) east of Ottawa

evidence.supports: Forest sits across the line between Clarence-Rockland and The Nation
evidence.quote: straddling the boundary of Clarence-Rockland and The Nation municipality

evidence.supports: Replanting project started in the 1920s, led by Ferdinand Larose
evidence.quote: a replanting project was initiated in the 1920s, spearheaded by Ferdinand Larose

evidence.supports: Area had been known as the Bourget Desert
evidence.quote: The area was then known as the Bourget Desert.

evidence.supports: In 1928 Larose persuaded the Russell County Council to buy 490 hectares
evidence.quote: In 1928, Larose persuaded the Russell County Council to purchase 490 hectares (1,200 acres)

evidence.supports: In 1928 the first 40 hectares were planted in red pine
evidence.quote: and that same year, the first 40 hectares (99 acres) were planted in red pine

evidence.supports: While the county owned the land, Ontario Department of Lands and Forests managed it
evidence.quote: management was the responsibility of Ontario Department of Lands and Forests

evidence.supports: Forest offers hiking, mountain biking, snowshoeing and cross-country skiing
evidence.quote: Recreational activities in the multi-purpose forest include hiking, mountain biking, snowshoeing and cross-country skiing
On the left is the Larose Tower circa June 1971.

evidence.supports: Tower was manned to protect the Larose Forest in the Kemptville District
evidence.quote: It was manned to protect the large Larose Forest in the Kemptville District, SE of Ottawa.

evidence.supports: Towers in use less from the 1960s as aerial spotting took over
evidence.quote: As the 1960's progressed the towers were in use less and less as aerial fire spotting and fire fighting crews took over.

evidence.supports: Fan guide lists a tower in the Larose Forest among popular originals that sightseers still use
evidence.quote: Some of the more popular originals still used by backwoods sightseers are situated at:

evidence.supports: Larose Forest tower is named in that list
evidence.quote: and the Larose Forest SE of Ottawa.

notes_for_editor: No build year or height in any source; the firelookout record shows N/A for tower type, height and year built. Tower facts come from a 1971 photo caption and a fan site. Forest history is from Wikipedia and is context, not tower history. A Facebook group post about a newer cupola could not be read, so it is not used. Current condition and access are unverified; check before publishing. Wikipedia says management of the forest reverted to the county in 2000; the story does not cover that.
